audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Yone levels 3 and 4-5 and Pantheon level 6, while the whys on the same page said 'Level 3 remains Pantheon's', 'Levels 4-5 even out into a skill check' and 'At 6 it's a skill check'. Four rows contradicted their own explanation text.
audit.why: The packet chart (Pantheon / Pantheon / Pantheon / Skill / Skill / Yone / Yone) matches the prose and the shape of the lane: Pantheon's kill pressure is levels 1-3, it evens out at 4-6, and Yone takes over from first item. The mirror deliberately left the chart untouched, so there is nothing to fight here.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 and 3 set to Pantheon, rows 4-5 and level 6 set to Skill, as matched full/content pairs with ratings and rewritten phases[].why lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield Vault, Comet Spear, Aegis Assault and Grand Starfall were all named without a single cooldown, and the packet counts only 2 sequencing cues on the whole page.
audit.why: Aegis Assault at 18-22s is by far his longest lane cooldown and is the real trade window; Shield Vault at 9-13s is the one to bait; Grand Starfall at 150-180s and 5500 range is a map tool, not a duel tool.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, phases[1].why, phases[2].why and phases[3].why, and Grand Starfall reframed as a roam in phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields claimed Pantheon's passive blocks your autos ('damage-blocking passive', 'Use his passive to block your key autos'). Mortal Will does no blocking — it empowers his next spell every few spells or attacks. The blocking belongs to Aegis Assault (E), and crucially it is invulnerability to damage FROM THE FRONT ONLY, which the page never said. Fate Sealed was again described as setting up knockups; it is a blink behind the last champion in a line plus a pull.
audit.why: Riot ability text in the brief. The front-only detail is the single most useful thing in this matchup for Yone, because Fate Sealed lands him behind the shield.
audit.corrected: Mortal Will restated as spell empowerment with the glow as the tell, Aegis Assault stated as frontal-only invulnerability with 'get behind it' as the counterplay, Shield Vault's auto-reset added as the burst tell, and Fate Sealed restated as blink-behind-and-pull.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Shield Vault's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

edits.before: Pantheon owns the early lane — his Q (Comet Spear) poke, W (Shield Vault) stun, and passive block against your first autos let him all-in you repeatedly; don't trade into his Q spam and respect the W-stun combo.
edits.after: Pantheon owns the early lane — Comet Spear (Q) pokes on 8-11s and Shield Vault (W) is a point-and-click dash stun on 9-13s that resets his auto; Mortal Will empowers his next spell, so watch the glow before you trade.

edits.before: Pantheon dominates the opening — his Comet Spear poke, Shield Vault stun, and damage-blocking passive let him all-in and out-trade you at every level 1-3 window. Play defensive, dodge his Q, and give up CS rather than health; do not fight into his stun.
edits.after: Pantheon dominates the opening — Comet Spear poke, a point-and-click Shield Vault stun, and Mortal Will empowering his next spell let him out-trade you at every level 1-3 window. Play defensive, dodge his Q, and give up CS rather than health; never fight into the stun.

edits.before: Use his passive to block your key autos in short trades
edits.after: Empower Mortal Will, then open with the Shield Vault stun

notes: Aegis Assault is invulnerability to damage FROM THE FRONT — nothing on the page said 'from the front', which is exactly the detail that makes Fate Sealed (a blink BEHIND the last champion in a line) the answer to it. Also fixed a straight kit error: Mortal Will was described twice as a passive that blocks your autos; it empowers his next spell. NOT EDITED: dontsFull[1].t reads 'Sit low for his W execute' — Shield Vault is a dash stun with no execute component, but the string is exactly 25 characters and near the applier's skip threshold, so the fix is recorded here rather than proposed.
